What happens when Mexican corridos meet shoegaze, nu-metal, and the experimental underground? For Henny Fay and Nico Malva of @corridosketamina, the result is a sound shaped by their different musical upbringings and a shared appetite for experimentation. Their new EP, Cktriz, pushes the project further into pop, incorporating 808s, hyperclash synths, and densely layered guitars alongside the traditional influences at its core. The duo has also developed a distinctive visual world with longtime friend and creative director Quetzi Morales, drawing on everything from early iPhone photography to fashion imagery. At the link in bio, Amanda Breeze talks to Corridos Ketamina about expanding the possibilities of regional Mexican music, embracing vulnerability, and building a world that feels entirely their own.⁣

Hat meter: from easy to hard. How far are you willing to venture?
There's inspiration everywhere.

Hats of all sorts emerged across SS27 collections from Vaquera’s exaggerated boaters to Matières Fécales feathered, canopied saucers. The leitmotif was sultry anonymity.

Hats hung perilously low, dangling just shy of the model’s eyelines cloaking their faces. The ostentatious hat becomes a personality proxy in an era where the face is the ultimate identifier, a way to be seen without being revealed. Swipe to explore.

Don't expect an immediate text back from Kelsey Lu (@iamkelseylu).⁣

The North Carolina-born singer, cellist, and composer has spent years moving between classical music, R&B, and experimental sound. Beyond music, there's plenty else to occupy the mind, from art that takes decades to appreciate to extraterrestrial-looking creatures.⁣

For SSMALL TALK, Lu gets into desire, childhood memories, personal boundaries, and more.

Umru helped throw a music festival in Minecraft that drew some 30,000 viewers and hosted the first-ever 100 gecs performance. Now 27, the producer and DJ has worked with Charli XCX, helped connect a generation of hyperpop artists, and brought his internet-born musical instincts onto the dancefloor. At the link in bio, A.M. Checchia meets @umru inside Minecraft to explore how an online community grew into a thriving real-world electronic music scene.⁣

It’s getting spooky. Whose "goth era" is your favorite?

Sophie Becker (@trophysophie) has strong feelings about objects. Some of them even have names.⁣
⁣
The performer counts her puppet Ronnie among the world's outstanding beauties and a household appliance among her favorite designs. Her new one-act satirical ventriloquist play, "Ronnie's Big Idea," shows that her taste is theatrical, a little uncanny, and not especially interested in conventional ideas of what looks good.⁣
⁣
For SSMALL TALK, we asked Becker about the things she finds beautiful, the art that changed her perspective, and what she’d like to wear next.
